civilopediaText.text: It moves low and fast along the tideline, more current than creature, closing the distance before its prey even registers the shape cutting through the shallows.
Fed well on whatever the tide brings in, this host has grown organs that were never meant to exist, built for exactly one purpose: to spit something corrosive at range.
Young, hungry, and already dangerous - it has learned that the fastest way to grow is to bring down anything that gallops too close to the water's edge.
A crude shell-plated frame, dragged along the shore by things that used to be beasts of burden, hurling barnacle-crusted shot at anything that stands between it and the water.

name: Floating Sea Drifter
uniques: Never appears as a Barbarian unit

civilopediaText.text: Not built so much as grown - a living hull of coral, chitin, and something that used to be a ship's crew, propelled by dozens of half-formed limbs beneath the waterline.

A hollow, discarded carapace reanimated and driven forward by something that no longer needs it to breathe. It skitters across open ground faster than anything with legs has a right to, striking hard before vanishing back toward the tideline.
This host stopped resembling anything human generations ago. What remains is pure appetite, wrapped in a shell hard enough to shrug off most blades.

name: Nethersea Spewer
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack

civilopediaText.text: Bloated far past any natural size, it exists only to hold pressure until it doesn't - and whatever it launches eats through stone almost as fast as it eats through flesh.
A long, barbed spine has grown clean through what was once an arm, and it has learned to whip it forward with enough force to punch through boiled leather.
Fed on the wreckage of a dozen raids, this carapace has swelled to the size of a warhorse, and moves with just as much murderous confidence.
Something in it has started to unravel rather than grow - limbs fusing wrong, instincts turning feral - but the spike jutting from its forelimb is more lethal than ever.
The barbed spine has grown into something closer to a siege weapon strapped to a living frame, cranked back by muscle that never seems to tire.
Layers of assimilated hosts have fused into one another, plated over with something dense and dark that turns aside steel edges without slowing down.

name: Nourished Spewer
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack

civilopediaText.text: It has learned to brace itself against rock rather than sand, giving whatever it launches enough range to reach over city walls before anyone inside knows it has arrived.
Grown larger and bolder now that it no longer needs to hide close to shore, this hull ranges further from home, dragging captured vessels down to add to its shape.
It does not fight so much as anchor - other hosts orient themselves around it, drawn to whatever signal it radiates from somewhere beneath its ribs.
What was once a runner has grown a single, terrible spine down its spine, angled forward - built to punch through anything else still foolish enough to charge.

name: Regressed Spewer
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack

civilopediaText.text: Whatever remained human in this host is long gone, replaced by something closer to a pressure vessel with legs, primed to unmake a wall in a single detonation.
Stripped down and skeletal, built purely for speed, it slips between patrol lanes to drag stragglers under before anyone can call for help.
It barely touches the surface, skipping across open water on fins that were never meant to move this fast, loosing pressurized bursts before the wake even settles.
The signal it carries has grown stronger, and stranger - nearby hosts move with unnerving coordination whenever it stands its ground.
Its charge has been clocked outrunning cavalry twice its size - the spine on its back has grown into something closer to a lance made of living bone.

name: Nethersea Brandguider
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack

civilopediaText.text: It does not aim so much as guide - other hosts nearby seem to know exactly where its payload will land, and get out of the way just in time.
Plated in something that isn't quite iron and isn't quite bone, it rams ships apart rather than sinking them, harvesting the wreckage as it goes.
It has stopped fighting for itself entirely - it exists now purely to relay the Voice, and the hosts around it fight harder for not understanding why.
Low, wide, and armored in overlapping plates, it drags itself forward on limbs that were never meant to bear this much weight, and crushes whatever it reaches.
Not a single creature but dozens of small ones acting as one, rising off the water in a shrieking column that scatters just as suddenly as it forms.
Larger than any ship it hunts, it no longer bothers hiding beneath the surface - it simply is the surface, for as long as it wants to be.
There is only ever one. Wherever it flies, smaller broodlings trail in its wake, dropped mid-flight and still forming by the time they land.
